column3: The Hebrew has field in the singular and all that is in it; BSB uses plural fields and them.
The Hebrew commands say; BSB expands this to cry out.
The Hebrew leaves David unnamed and repeats before the ark as the place of service; BSB supplies David and uses there for the second location.
The Hebrew says their brothers, sixty-eight; BSB describes them as his sixty-eight relatives.
The Hebrew continues the preceding appointment without naming David again and calls the priests his brothers; BSB repeats David and uses fellow priests.
The Hebrew describes what the LORD commanded concerning Israel without a separate keeping verb; BSB supplies to keep.
